title: POC integration planning: OpenAI-compat SDK + structured output with Borealis Retail
summary: POC scoping focused on validating OpenAI-compatible SDK integration, structured JSON outputs for downstream order-assist tooling, and workload benchmarks for mid-tier retail traffic. Agreed target success criteria (latency, throughput, correctness), a 6-week pilot timeline with a 2-week bench sprint, and next steps to run a baseline benchmark and share security docs. Action items assigned for bench scripts, infra config, and pricing follow-up.
topics: benchmark plan (seq len, q8 quant, batching)
function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs
deployment mode: hosted vs private VPC
next_steps: Redwood to send POC SOW and pricing sheet (Leah) - due 2027-06-08
SE to provide benchmark harness and initial scripts (Sameer) - due 2027-06-07
Borealis infra to stand up test VPC and share access controls (Priya) - due 2027-06-10
Customer to provide 2 sample prompt sets and data schemas (Maya) - due 2027-06-06
action_items: Leah Park: Draft SOW + pilot pricing and share via Doc - 2027-06-08
Sameer Patel: Deliver benchmark harness (locally runnable script + sample workloads) - 2027-06-07
Priya Kapoor: Provision test VPC and IAM roles, share IP allowlist - 2027-06-10
Maya Chen: Provide canonical prompt sets and expected structured JSON schema - 2027-06-06
Samir Bose: Export 48h anonymized traffic traces for sizing (seq len histograms) - 2027-06-09
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03 11:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Leah Park (Redwood AE), Sameer Patel (Redwood SE), Hannah Liu (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Borealis Head of ML), Oliver Grant (Eng Mgr), Priya Kapoor (Head of Infra), Samir Bose (Lead DE)

Summary (auto): Quick alignment on POC goals, bench plan, and integration approach. Agreed 6-week pilot with two bench sprints then a production readiness gate.

[00:00:00] Leah (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, we have Sameer on for technical, Hannah for customer success; Maya, Oliver, Priya, Samir from Borealis?
[00:00:12] Maya (Borealis): Yep, hi all. Excited to kick this off.
[00:00:18] Oliver (Borealis): Morning. Quick note, schedule's tight so we want to be pragmatic about success criteria.
[00:00:25] Leah: Totally. The goal today is to lock success criteria, workload sizing, and an integration plan — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling and structured outputs. We'll also agree a bench plan.
[00:00:40] Sameer (Redwood SE): I'll cover how the SDKs fit into your stack, the benchmark harness we propose, and what telemetry we'll need to validate.
[00:00:48] Priya: For infra, our main questions are around network (VPC peering vs public endpoints), KMS, and audit logs. SOC2 is table stakes for us.
[00:00:56] Leah: Great, we'll cover that. To start: Maya, can you describe the user flow you'll pilot?
[00:01:05] Maya: Sure — we're building an order-assist agent for store associates. Typical prompt is a short product search + context (inventory, store id). Response needs to be structured — SKU list, quantities, reason codes — JSON schema that our POS can ingest. Latency target is interactive: p95 under 300ms ideally, but we can accept up to 500ms for complex queries.
[00:01:28] Samir: Traffic profile for peak: about 200 qps on promos, average seq len ~ 350 tokens, tail to 800 tokens for multi-item queries. That's 9–11 tokens per word approximate.
[00:01:42] Sameer: OK that helps. For the POC we typically bench at representative seq lengths: 128, 350, and 800. We recommend the baseline at 350 since it's your median.
[00:01:54] [00:02:00] Oliver: Cost is a big lever. We need unit economics that make sense — we're targeting under $X per 1k requests, or per 1M tokens — we'll take your pricing but need ways to control costs.
[00:02:12] Leah: We'll provide a modeled estimate in the SOW across options: hosted Redwood, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC. Also suggestions on quantization (e.g., Q4/Q8) and batching policies.
[00:02:24] Sameer: For throughput/latency tradeoffs, we'll propose two configs: low-latency (smaller batch, higher cost) and cost-optimized (aggressive batching + prefix caching). We'll show batch-sizing curves from our runtime.
[00:02:40] Maya: About structured output — can Redwood enforce schema and validate? We need deterministic JSON keys for downstream ingestion and confidence scores per field.
[00:02:49] Sameer: Yes, we support structured-output constraints and can add a lightweight schema enforcement step in the runtime via response validators. We also emit per-field confidence and token-level traces. Note: sometimes the transcription layer mislabels names — but we do have token alignments.
[00:03:05] [00:03:15] Priya: What about function/tool calling? We want the model to call inventory lookup APIs and then return the combined JSON. Can that live inside the same pipeline?
[00:03:25] Sameer: Absolutely. We map OpenAI-style tool calls into our SDK hooks. You'd declare a tool (inventory_lookup) that returns structured payload; Redwood's runtime can orchestrate a synchronous tool call and feed results back into the model for final structured output.
[00:03:39] Maya: Any gotchas? We have rate-limited inventory APIs.
[00:03:44] Sameer: We'll instrument timeouts and retries and can do speculative calls — e.g., return best-effort fields with a partial flag if tool times out. Also, can fall back to cached KV lookups for hot SKUs.
[00:03:54] [00:04:00] Oliver: Security — we need KMS integration, key rotation, and full audit logs. Will Redwood Private or Dedicated give us that?
[00:04:08] Leah: Private gives you customer-controlled KMS and VPC-only control plane. Dedicated supports customer-managed keys for payload encryption and extended audit retention as an add-on. We'll include the security spec in the doc.
[00:04:20] Hannah: I'll attach SOC2 and our compliance pack after this call.
[00:04:24] Maya: Great. On benchmarks, what metrics will you produce?
[00:04:30] Sameer: We'll provide end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token throughput, token efficiency (tokens/sec per GPU), cost-per-1M-tokens estimate per config, and quality metrics: schema adherence rate, field-level accuracy measured against ground truth.
[00:04:44] Samir: For field accuracy we'll need labeled pairs; Maya can provide ~500 annotated examples for the initial run.
[00:04:53] Maya: We can do that. We'll annotate SKU lists and expected JSON.
[00:04:58] [00:05:00] Leah: TIMELINE proposal: Week 0 (this week) — agreement and SOW. Weeks 1–2 — bench sprint: infra, benchmark harness, and baseline runs. Weeks 3–4 — integration sprint (tool calling, schema validation), Weeks 5–6 — hardened pilot + run production-ish traffic and final gating decision.
[00:05:20] Oliver: That sounds reasonable. Can we do a hard gating criterion at the end: p95 < 300ms on median workload, schema adherence > 98%, and cost within the modeled threshold?
[00:05:30] Leah: Yes, we'll bake those into the SOW as acceptance criteria.
[00:05:35] [00:05:45] Priya: On the bench harness — will it run in our VPC or using Redwood tooling? We prefer to run tests from our infra to measure real network effects.
[00:05:54] Sameer: We can support both. For initial runs we usually run a hybrid: seed tests from Redwood-hosted infra to validate runtime config, then run a client-run from your VPC to capture network latency. We'll hand you the harness (python script + docker image).
[00:06:10] Maya: What's required from our side for the harness?
[00:06:14] Sameer: You'll need a small VM to run the script, access credentials (we'll provide short-lived), and sample prompt sets plus expected JSON. We'll also need seq length histograms and a peak qps estimate (you gave 200).
[00:06:26] [00:06:30] Leah: For SDKs — are you leaning to embed Redwood's client or prefer HTTP OpenAI-compatible endpoints?
[00:06:36] Oliver: We prefer to keep it OpenAI-compatible so we can swap in/out if later needed.
[00:06:40] Leah: Good. Redwood supports both: an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint and official SDKs (JS/Python/Go). Function-calling semantics follow OpenAI-style signatures; our SDK adds helpers for schema enforcement and per-field confidence.
[00:06:54] Maya: For streaming — we need partial results for UX. Is streaming supported with schema enforcement?
[00:07:00] Sameer: We support streaming tokens while still performing post-hoc schema validation. For UX, we can stream a preliminary JSON plus a final validation patch. There's some complexity if you rely on strict ordering, but we've done this before. Expect occasional retractions for malformed fields.
[00:07:16] [00:07:30] Priya: Any special network ports or firewall rules for Private?
[00:07:34] Leah: For Private we'll provide a Control Plane endpoint accessible via peered VPC or private link; data plane stays in your VPC. We'll send a minimal network matrix, but typically you open egress to Redwood ingestion IPs during benching and configure a NAT for the control channel.
[00:07:50] Samir: Also, we'll need an allowlist for the bench runner if you're running tests from your environment.
[00:07:55] Maya: About model versions — will we be able to pin a model family? We want to test a smaller quantized variant for cost runs and a full-fidelity variant for accuracy runs.
[00:08:03] Sameer: Yes. You can pin by version. We recommend starting with a high-quality fp16/8-bit mix for accuracy runs, then Q8 and Q4 for cost-optimized. We'll present expected quality deltas from prior benchmarks.
[00:08:17] [00:08:30] Oliver: For telemetry — do you provide token-level traces and per-request cost breakdown so we can annotate our own metrics?
[00:08:36] Hannah: We provide per-request token counts, model variant used, runtime batch size, and cost breakdown. We'll share a sample CSV schema.
[00:08:44] Maya: Great. One operational concern: multi-tenant noise. If we use hosted during POC, will noisy neighbors affect latency?
[00:08:52] Leah: Hosted can have variability; Dedicated gives capacity isolation. For POC, we can simulate consistent load; if you want strict isolation we recommend Dedicated pilot or Private deployment. We'll model both.
[00:09:05] [00:09:15] Samir: Bench specifics: We'll run bench across 3 axes: sequence length (128/350/800), concurrency (1/10/50 simulated clients), and model variant (fp16, q8, q4). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and schema adherence for each cell. For cost runs we'll compute cost per 1M tokens extrapolated to your traffic.
[00:09:36] Maya: OK. How long do the bench runs take?
[00:09:40] Sameer: A full grid run typically takes 4–8 hours per model variant. We'll prioritize the median cell first to get quick feedback within 24–48 hours.
[00:09:51] [00:10:00] Priya: Are there examples of similar retailers you can share (anonymized) for SLOs and cost baselines?
[00:10:06] Leah: We can provide anonymized bench snapshots and unit economics; I'll include a sanitized benchmark deck.
[00:10:12] Maya: About data retention and logs — we need to ensure PII never leaves our environment for some flows.
[00:10:18] Leah: Under Private you can restrict logging and set zero-logging for those flows. For hosted, we have redaction and opt-out flags, but Private is the sure route for strict PII requirements.
[00:10:29] [00:10:45] Oliver: Let's discuss success criteria specifics so the SOW can include numbers: we propose p95 < 300ms for median workload, schema adherence >= 98%, field-level precision >= 95% for SKU quantities, and cost not to exceed X in the model.
[00:10:58] Sameer: Agreed. We'll quantify cost as modeled dollars per 1M tokens for each config and include thresholds for acceptance. For the schema test we'll need your labeled dataset.
[00:11:08] Maya: We'll assign a small team to label 500 examples.
[00:11:12] [00:11:20] Leah: Next steps recap: Sameer will drop the benchmark harness; Leah will send SOW/pricing and security pack; Priya will provision test network; Maya will provide prompts and labels; Samir will export seq histograms.
[00:11:34] Priya: Timeline check — can we start bench runs next Monday (2027-06-07)?
[00:11:38] Leah: Yes, that's our goal. We'll aim to deliver harness by end-of-week so you can stand up the runner.
[00:11:46] [00:11:55] Hannah: I'll create a shared folder and upload the SOC2 + compliance docs and the sample bench template.
[00:12:00] Oliver: One more question — fallback behavior in outages: can Redwood route to a cheaper model or degrade gracefully?
[00:12:08] Sameer: Yes. We support routing policies — you can fallback to a distilled variant, or to a cached prefix result. We can configure time-based fallback thresholds.
[00:12:18] Maya: For function calling, we want to see a short demo. Can you schedule a 45-minute deep-dive to wire up an inventory API and show end-to-end?
[00:12:25] Leah: Absolutely — we'll schedule a separate SE-led workshop next week.
[00:12:30] [00:12:45] Action recap (verbal):
- Redwood: SOW, pricing, bench harness, compliance pack
- Borealis: labels, seq histograms, infra for runner

[00:12:58] Oliver: Thanks, this is very helpful.
[00:13:02] Maya: Quick note — when you share the harness, please include a small dataset seed so we can validate the harness runs out-of-the-box.
[00:13:09] Sameer: Will do. We'll include a docker image and a minimal dataset (50 examples) so you can run a smoke test.
[00:13:16] Leah: Any other questions?
[00:13:20] Priya: Nothing from infra.
[00:13:22] Samir: All good.
[00:13:24] [00:13:30] Leah: OK thanks everyone — we'll follow up with SOW and set up the demo.
[00:13:35] Meeting ends.
notes: Customer emphasized strict schema enforcement and field-level confidence
Agreement on 6-week pilot with bench sprint in weeks 1–2
Redwood to provide hybrid bench harness (hosted+client-run)
Private deployment recommended if PII cannot leave customer environment
